title: US markets closed — Christmas Day observed (Friday 2027-12-24; no December early close in 2027, and 12-31 stays a full session)
source: NEWS: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200 after its 302 -- the page needs curl -L -- 109,180 bytes) and parsed cell by cell by this session, the same artifact and byte count the thanksgiving-market-closure-2027-11-25 proposal already records. The page states "All NYSE markets observe U.S. holidays as listed below for 2026, 2027, and 2028"; its Christmas Day row parses as ["Friday, December 25****", "Friday, December 24 (Christmas Day observed)", "Monday, December 25"] for 2026 / 2027 / 2028, so 2027 is a FULL closure on Friday December 24. THE SAME ROW SETTLES THE OTHER HALF OF THE 2027 YEAR-END WEEK: footnote **** names exactly ONE December early close across all three years -- "Thursday, December 24, 2026" -- so December 2027 has no 1:00 p.m. session at all, and footnote * reads verbatim "Because the holiday falls on Saturday, January 1, 2028, no New Year Day holiday is observed", which keeps Friday 2027-12-31 a full session. INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED FROM A SECOND, NON-EXCHANGE PRIMARY fetched the same session: the OCC own 2027 expiration calendar (www.optionseducation.org/api/expirationcalendar, HTTP 200, 34,871 bytes) carries {"date":"2027-12-24T00:00:00","holiday":{"description":"Exchange/OCC holiday","hatched":true}} and marks no other late-December 2027 date that way. REPRODUCED A THIRD TIME MECHANICALLY, FROM A SESSION RECORD RATHER THAN A CALENDAR: Christmas Day 2027 falls on a Saturday, and in every prior Saturday-Christmas year -- 1993, 1999, 2004, 2010 and 2021, 5 of 5 -- December 24 is ABSENT from CBOE own VIX_History.csv index history (9,267 sessions, 1990-01-02 to 2026-09-07) while December 23 and December 27 are both present. Filed estimate on the same two counts every sibling closure entry documents (labor-day-market-closure-2026-09-07, good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26, memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31, thanksgiving-market-closure-2027-11-25): the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an exchange own holiday calendar, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE is not in doubt -- the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Discovered during the fhfa-hpi-2027-12-28 initial research, checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the fhfa-hpi-2027-12-28 initial research (2026-09-08), where it is load-bearing rather than incidental: that ledger third leg measures the year-end volatility regime by TRADING-SESSION COUNT (the last five sessions of the year) rather than by calendar date, because the session-count definition separates about four times more sharply (VIX9D/VIX p=0.0016, seed-stable 0.0013-0.0019, n=75, against p=0.0065 for the calendar-date Dec 24-31 window the fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29 lane used). Which sessions those are in 2027 depends entirely on this closure. WITH 2027-12-24 CLOSED AND 2027-12-31 OPEN, the last five sessions of 2027 are December 27, 28, 29, 30 and 31 -- five full sessions, none of them an early close -- so the FHFA print on 2027-12-28 is the SECOND of the five and the fourth from the year end, matching the 2021, 2022 and 2023 configurations exactly. THE HOLE IT FILLS: this calendar tracks christmas-eve-half-day-2026-12-24 -- an EARLY CLOSE -- but no Christmas CLOSURE entry in any year, while carrying full-closure entries for Labor Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, MLK, Presidents Day and Washington Birthday, and a proposed one for Thanksgiving 2027. The id follows that class convention, <holiday>-market-closure-<date>, not the half-day one -- and the distinction is the point here, because 2027 is a closure where 2026 is a half day. THREE NOTES FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT. (1) The 2028 Christmas closure (Monday, December 25) is in the same table and is deliberately NOT proposed -- one file per finding, and this lane needs 2027. (2) Unlike an event resting on a tentative schedule, this date inherits no chain: a Saturday-Christmas observance is a fixed rule reproduced 5 of 5 from a session record, so it can promote on its own initial research the moment a lane finds a prefix the taxonomy accepts. (3) A closure four days ahead of the FHFA print is the reason the 2027 year-end week has no half day in it, which matters to any intraday design run on that week -- the 09:00 ET pre-market bar this chain now uses exists only on full sessions. IMPACT low matches every sibling closure entry. symbols is empty; a closure removes sessions, it does not signal. Proposed as an estimate; estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
